# Dry-test matrix — what each driver's suite notices

<!-- Generated by `node tools/seed-defects/matrix.mjs` from reference/reports/seed-defects.json, tools/seed-defects/ and
     tools/seed-defects/applicability.json. Do not edit: CI fails when this disagrees with them. -->

Item 12.C.2–3 of `DRY-COVERAGE-PLAN.md`. **This page measures the suites, not the robots.** For each driver, realistic defects — each
one of a kind that has really happened to a driver in this repository (`tools/seed-defects/classes.json`) — were put into a temporary
copy of it, one at a time, and the strongest suite that runs without hardware was run. A defect the suite goes red on is **noticed**; one
it does not is a **survivor**: a defect of that kind that would reach a robot. Every driver also carries a **control** — a defect no dry suite
can see — which must survive, so that a rate which cannot fall is not mistaken for a suite that cannot miss.

What the numbers are not: a probability that a driver works (no such number exists from here, and the plan refuses to print one); a
claim that no other defect is present (the seeds were authored, and the ones nobody thought of are not in the count); or a statement
about the counterpart the suite runs against, whose own correctness is what the release stage (`alpha`, `beta`) is about. **Rung** is
F118's: 1 the maker's controller software, 2 the maker's simulator, 3 an independent implementation, 4 a counterpart written in this
repository. A hermetic suite is rung 4 by construction, so a beta driver's hermetic rate understates it: the survivors are re-run at the
rung its stage rests on (`--rung N --survivors-of 4`) and the stronger result is the one in the class table.

Reproduce: `node tools/seed-defects/seed-defects.mjs --driver <name> --report` (WSL or Linux; `SEED_PYTHON_REQUESTS` and `SEED_PYTHON_SPOT` name
the interpreters that carry `requests` and `bosdyn-client`). `--check` says whether every seed still applies exactly once.

6546 seeded defects across 34 drivers; 129 class-by-driver cells unseeded and 64 stated not applicable.

## Drivers that command a robot and have no hermetic suite here

* `booster-k1` — the K1 is the Booster driver's library told `model: k1`, so its defects are seeded in the Booster set (`seeds/booster.json` carries the K1's tables, names, roles, body selection and layout beside the T1's, and the seeded suite runs the K1's path too): there is no second set to run.

## Survivors

Each row is a defect of a kind that has happened, put into the driver, that the driver's suite at its strongest measured rung did **not** notice. It is a
test to write, or — where the note says so — a defect that rung cannot observe and a higher one can. A survivor is a finding, not a score to defend.

### `onrobot` at rung 4: 1 survivor

| Seed | Class | The defect | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `onrobot-txn-write-line` | `request-reply-wedge` | a write made without the line's lock |  |

### `rainbow` at rung 4: 1 survivor

| Seed | Class | The defect | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rainbow-events-notify` | `jitter-as-stall` | an event does not wake what waits for a reading |  |

## Controls, and differences no test at the driver's rung can see (left out of every rate)

Each is a real difference that the suite is **expected** not to notice: a control is how a rate that cannot fall is caught (class `undetectable`), and any other row is a survivor triaged as unreachable at this rung, with the reason. They are listed so the rate is not read as covering them.

| Driver | Seed | Class | The difference | Why no test sees it |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `booster` | `boo-write-failure-ignored` | `ack-then-fault` | a publish the channel refused reported as sent: the hold and setpoint records advance for a command that never went out | a defect this rung cannot observe: the vendor's `Write` returns false only if the channel refuses the sample, which a fake on the same loopback never makes it do. |
| `booster` | `boo-control-open-poll` | `undetectable` | CONTROL: the interval at which open() looks for the first state. Ten milliseconds of latency on a session that takes seconds to start | a control: only a real controller or a real clock could tell |
| `booster` | `boo-control-open-deadline` | `undetectable` | CONTROL: how long open() waits for a first state before it gives up. A suite that always finds the robot publishing never reaches it | a control: only a real controller or a real clock could tell |
| `booster` | `boo-control-interval-kept-across-sessions` | `undetectable` | CONTROL: the measured publication interval carried into the next session. The same robot publishes at the same rate, and the wait is the watchdog window unless the robot is slower than fifty hertz, which the fake is not | a control: only a real controller or a real clock could tell |
| `canopen` | `canopen-sdo-timeout-control` | `undetectable` | CONTROL: how long an SDO waits for a drive that never answers. Nothing asserts the number, so the suite is merely slower on a silent drive | a control: only a real controller or a real clock could tell |
| `canopen-rs` | `cnr-poll-control` | `undetectable` | CONTROL: how long one poll inside an SDO wait lasts. Only a real bus's timing could tell 10 ms from 11 | a control: only a real controller or a real clock could tell |
| `canopen-rs` | `cnr-stop-first-error` | `stop-path` | a stop that gives up at the first failed write: the axes after it keep running | a real difference that no test at this rung can see: every quick-stop and the NMT frame go out on one raw socket, so a write that fails at the first axis fails at every one after it (the interface is down, or the queue is full), and there is nothing the later axes would have sent that one which carried on would not also have lost. A seam that failed one write and let the next through would make it observable, and this port does not carry one. The loop that attempts every axis is read in the source. |
| `canopen-rs` | `cnr-stop-contended-ok` | `sticky-error` | a stop that could not take the stop path's lock says it delivered | a real difference that no deterministic test at this rung can see: the stop path's lock is held only by open and close, for microseconds, so contention cannot be arranged without a seam in the lock (a test-only hook this port does not carry). The refusal is one line, EIO rather than OK, and is read in the source. |
| `canopen-rs` | `cnr-latch-recheck` | `stop-path` | the latch not re-checked under the body's lock: a command that passed the first check while a stop landed races onto the bus (a race no sequential test forces) | a real difference that no deterministic test can see: it needs a stop to land in the few instructions between the first latch check and taking the body lock, and the only way to hold that window open is a seam in the lock or a stress run, which would be a flake (F187). The re-check closes the race and is read in the source. |
| `dobot` | `dobot-link-nodelay-off` | `undetectable` | Nagle's algorithm left on: each small command may wait for an acknowledgement, which only a real network shows | a control: only a real controller or a real clock could tell |
| `ethercat` | `ecat-sm-length-control` | `undetectable` | CONTROL: a reserved byte of the sync-manager registers, written non-zero. The suite's slave ignores a reserved field, and so does a real one | a control: only a real controller or a real clock could tell |
| `ethercat-rs` | `ecr-stop-contended-ok` | `sticky-error` | a stop that could not take the stop path's lock says it delivered | a real difference that no deterministic test at this rung can see: the stop path's lock is held only by open and close, for microseconds, so contention cannot be arranged without a seam in the lock (a test-only hook this port does not carry). The refusal is one line, EIO rather than OK, and is read in the source. |

## Equivalent mutants (left out of every rate)

A change nothing observable differs by cannot be noticed by any test, so it is not a gap. Each carries its reason, and must still survive: one that a suite kills was not equivalent.

| Driver | Seed | Class | Why nothing observable differs |
|---|---|---|---|
| `canopen-rs` | `cnr-write-latch-check` | `stop-path` | the re-check under the body lock, which this leaves in place, refuses a command while the latch is set with the same status, and the first check is an early return that saves taking the lock: results are the same and only the wait for the lock differs, which no caller can tell. |
